steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease the bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix graham cracker crumbs and melted butter together in a bowl until evenly moistened. Press crumb mixture into the bottom and about 1/2 inch up the sides of the springform pan.
Whisk sour cream, flour, and vanilla extract together in a bowl; set aside.

Stir cream cheese and sugar together with a wooden spoon in a separate bowl until evenly incorporated, 3 to 5 minutes; add milk and whisk until just combined. Whisk in eggs, one at a time, stirring well after each addition. Stir in lemon zest, orange zest, and sour cream mixture; whisk until just incorporated.
Pour mixture into prepared springform pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until the edges have nicely puffed and the surface of the cheesecake is firm except for a small spot in the center that will jiggle when the pan is gently shaken, about 1 hour.
When the cheesecake is done, turn off the oven and let it cool in the oven for 3 to 4 hours. This prevents any cracks from forming on the top of the cheesecake.

raw_recipe.headline: New York-Style Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This foolproof New York cheesecake recipe from Chef John makes a rich and delicious dense cheesecake infused with orange, lemon, and vanilla.

review.reviewBody: One of the best I have made or tasted. A real family hit! The only change made was I made my graham cracker crust a bit different, but all in all followed the receipe and it turned out perfect.

Made this recipie multiple times. I would suggest using a 1” bigger pan, add some cinnamon, and use a water bath to prevent cracks. I put my pan on a small rack in a large roasting pan, to keep the spring pan above the water. Also, add an entire stick of butter to the graham cracker crust. Adheres much better. I use crisco to line the interior top to bottom. Works great.

I used this recipe as a starting point to make a gluten and dairy free cheesecake. I made quite a few alterations like using lactose-free cream cheese spread and whipped coconut cream with lemon juice instead of sour cream. I also added crushed pecans and ginger to my gluten free graham cracker crust. It came out amazing. I read a comment on here with a tip to put a tray of water on the bottom rack great tip! I also like to tap the cheesecake on the counter and let it sit for a minute before baking to get the air bubbles out. 3 hours to cool down in the oven, then 1 hr in the fridge to chill.

This recipe was a great success! Everyone raved about it. The only change I made was adding the juice of one lemon, because I like lemon. I also added more butter to the crust and added 1/3 cup sugar . Fabulous texture. Yes, I will make it again. Next time I will leave out the zest and just use 2tsp vanilla for something different with cherry topping. The top did not crack after 4 hours cooling in the oven. I cooled another hour on the counter.

This is an amazing tasting cheesecake! I’ve made it three times already in a one month. The only change I made was to add Splenda instead of sugar as my husband is diabetic. I honestly couldn’t taste a difference. I did put a pan of water on the bottom shelf in the oven to prevent cracking. It worked! Good job once again, Chef John!

This recipe is incredibly good. Rave reviews from my guests! Like many of the other reviewers stated, the graham crackers w/ butter needed a size modification. I used 7 oz. of graham crackers with 5 T of butter and it made a perfect crust. I used Trader Joe's cinnamon crackers and they needed no other additions. I cooked the rest of the recipe the same as specified but added 15 minutes since it really was too wet to pull sooner. I only left the oven closed after cooking for one hour then cooled it on the counter, waiting till it was @ 65 degrees temp before refrigerating for 5 hours. It did crack the middle but not horribly. I took it out of the fridge 1.5 hours before serving. This is now my favorite cheesecake recipe!

Def a keeper. I omitted the citrus; mine was a salted caramel cheesecake so I thought plain would taste better with those toppings. I also baked it in a cheesecake bath. No cracks! Thanks for the tips on preparation ... i think hand mixing did help in achieving the perfect texture and beautiful, smooth top. Enjoyed by all; tasted as good as it looked!

I put 5 blocks of cream cheese and 5 eggs separating the yokes and whites yokes in first and used lady fingers instead of gram cracker and mine was twice as high as the picture, plus I used my kitchen aid mixer instead of the by hand method and used a water bath.

This was a delicious recipe, super easy to make! That said, I did/will tweak a few small things. One, while the flavor was delicious, I might put a little less sour cream next time, as the flavor was a little much. Two, add more butter to the crumbs to make them bind (I think I used 6 Tbsp). I also had only crumbs (not whole graham crackers) and ended up using 2 cups, which was perfect. Mine needed to bake longer than 1 hour and ended up mushy in the middle, so next time I would add 10 or so minutes to it.

My family loves this cheesecake!! My daughter wants it every year for her birthday. I too had to much Graham cracker, not enough butter for my crust. I have made this probably ten times and just realized tonight that I'm using too many Graham crackers. I was using 18 full crackers. I think it means for you to use 18 of the squares.... I omit the citrus usually as well. Mine usually cracks, but we don't care. The first time I made it, I joked that it wanted to be pi! See photo

Excellent recipe, I’ve made several versions of cheesecakes before, but I needed to check what I needed as I recently relocated out of the country. The only thing different I normally do that I’d suggest here is a way to prevent cracks. Not only cooling on the oven, but I bake my cheesecake in a water bath. I take my springform pan, and wrap the bottom in foil (leaving the top exposed) then place the whole pan in a larger baking pan filled with water. This baked the cake a bit more gently and lets it cook more gently so cracks are far less common. Also, I add eggs at the end, as eggs tend to hold air and less mixing with the eggs means less air, and the air pockets also cause cracks.
Superb , it came out perfect . I do put a sheet pan filled with water while cooking it keeps the cheesecake firm and won’t crack
This cheesecake is so good. My family loves it.

This recipe was beyond amazing! I usually make a cheesecake for our family get together, and decided to try this version - just a little different than what I normally make. It was a BIG HIT!! My pan isn't really deep, though...so I ended up dividing into two pans....they turned out perfectly! Definitely a keeper! Y U M!
So I made this dessert for Christmas dinner and it was fairly simple to prepare and my family loves it

I made this to the recipe except I uses cinnamon graham crackers. Its in the oven now. It smells so good. Topping it with strawberry topping. I can't wait to taste it tomorrow at the family Christmas party.
Need 2 sticks of butter melted for 18 full graham crackers.

I made this gluten-free, and it turned out amazing. I used gluten-free vanilla wafer cookies (2 boxes) and 2 sticks of butter for the crust and all-purpose gluten-free flour. Everything else was the same and it was the best cheesecake I have ever had. My family agreed and they are not gluten-free. Will be making it again.

This is an excellent cheesecake! I do agree with the other reviewers that 3 tbsps of melted butter to 18 crushed graham crackers makes for a very dry crust. It needs either more butter, or less crackers to make it work. I also thought the cheesecake itself was a little on the sweet side for my tastes. I would probably leave out the orange zest, use less sugar, and add some lemon juice next time. Otherwise, the texture of this cheesecake is phenomenal, and I love that it doesn't require a water bath! Thanks for the recipe, Chef John!

I didn’t add the lemon or orange zest because I used chocolate graham crackers for my crust. I didn’t make in a water bath and did wind up with some cracks. I followed everything else and it turned out great. The taste is not as rich as some cheesecakes and it was very good! Thank you for the recipe!
